summary: Add a tamper‑evident ledger that records every receipt and mileage change, import existing data as ledger entries on first launch, expose a History view for each record, show ledger verification status in Settings, implement verifiable CSV/PDF exports with ledger entries, and enforce ledger verification on backup/restore. Update the UI flow to include the History screen and Settings status.
steps: 1. Create src/lib/ledger.ts containing types for LedgerEntry, functions to append entries (appendLedgerEntry), compute the next seq, getPrevHash, canonical JSON (deterministic field order, no whitespace), and hash calculation using @noble/hashes/sha2.js (sha256) and utils (bytesToHex, utf8ToBytes). Export appendEntryForReceipt(kind, recordId, data) and appendEntryForMileage(kind, recordId, data).

2. Add src/lib/ledgerHelpers.ts with helpers: getLedger(store) → LedgerEntry[], setLedger(store, entries) (stores encrypted JSON array), initLedgerIfNeeded(store) → runs on app start; if ledger key missing, loads all existing receipts and mileage entries via receiptStore.getAll... and mileageStore.getAll..., creates a single 'imported' entry per record (kind='imported', at=importDate, data=full record, prevHash = last hash, hash computed). Marks a flag in store (e.g., 'ledgerImported' = true) to ensure it runs only once.

3. Add src/lib/ledgerVerification.ts exposing verifyLedger(store) → { ok: boolean, entries: LedgerEntry[], firstBadSeq?: number, reason?: string }. Re‑computes hash chain, checks seq continuity, prevHash matching, and returns first bad entry if any.

4. Update src/lib/receiptStore.ts: after each successful addReceipt, editReceipt, deleteReceipt (or similar functions), call the appropriate ledger helper: appendEntryForReceipt('receipt.created', receipt.id, receipt) etc. Ensure the edit flow uses kind 'receipt.corrected' and delete uses 'receipt.deleted'. Include OCR pre‑fill data in the data object for created/corrected entries when applicable.

5. Update src/lib/mileageStore.ts similarly: after addMileageEntry, editMileageEntry, deleteMileageEntry, call appendEntryForMileage with kinds 'mileage.created', 'mileage.corrected', 'mileage.deleted'.

6. Extend src/lib/backup.ts: when creating a backup, include the current ledger entries (store under a top‑level 'ledger' field). When restoring, after decrypting the backup, call verifyLedger on the restored ledger; if !ok, throw an error with a friendly message. If the backup lacks a ledger (legacy backup), treat all restored receipts/mileage as 'imported' by invoking initLedgerIfNeeded on the restored store after import.

7. Modify src/lib/exportCsv.ts: after generating the CSV string, compute verificationCode = first 12 hex chars of SHA‑256 over csvContentWithoutVerificationLine. Append a line: "# verification: entries=<N>, headHash=<HEAD_HASH>, code=<CODE>". Then call ledger.appendEntryForExport('export.created', { format: 'csv', code, entries: N, headHash }). Adjust exportPdf similarly (add code line at end of PDF text and ledger entry kind 'export.created' with format='pdf').
8. Create UI components:
- src/components/ui/HistoryItem.tsx: renders a single ledger entry (date, kind, optional data preview).
- src/components/ui/HistoryList.tsx: lists entries sorted by seq ascending (newest last).
- src/components/ui/VerificationStatus.tsx: shows "Verified • N entries • intact" or warning with firstBadSeq and reason.
9. Add History screens:

- src/screens/ReceiptHistoryScreen.tsx: receives receiptId via route params, loads ledger via ledger.getLedger(store), filters entries where recordId matches receiptId and kind starts with 'receipt.', passes them to HistoryList. Include a back button.
- src/screens/MileageHistoryScreen.tsx: analogous for mileage records.
- Add navigation entries for these screens in src/navigation/index.tsx (push onto stack from ReceiptEntryScreen and MileageEntryScreen via a "History" button).

10. Update SettingsScreen.tsx: import verifyLedger, call it on mount, store result in component state, render VerificationStatus component showing ledger status. Add a button "Verify an export" that navigates to VerifyExportScreen.

11. Create VerifyExportScreen.tsx: UI to either pick a CSV file (using expo-document-picker) or input a PDF verification code. For CSV: read the file, strip the verification line, recompute the 12‑char code, locate the matching ledger entry (kind='export.created' and same code). If found, display whether the file matches (hashes identical), whether any records were corrected/deleted after that export (by checking ledger entries with seq > entry.seq and same recordId types). For PDF code: just search ledger for entry.format='pdf' with that code and show same info. If not found, show "code not from this app".
12. Update ui_flow.json: extend the primary flow (edit receipt) to include opening the History screen and seeing the correction entry, and add a step in Settings to display the verified status.
13. Ensure all new files export their functions and are imported where needed. Update any barrel files (src/lib/index.ts if exists) to re‑export ledger utilities.
14. Add unit tests (already covered in the acceptance test script) that:
- Verify hash chaining and canonical JSON produce expected hash.
- detect a changed field, removed entry, reordered entry, changed prevHash and report first bad seq.
- ensure corrections keep the original entry in the chain.
- confirm import runs only once on first launch.
- generate a CSV export, verify the verification line, then alter one character and ensure verification fails and reports records changed after later corrections.
- verify a typed PDF code is found in the ledger and reports correct export info.
- report an unknown code as not from this app.
- backup round‑trip retains a verifying ledger, and a tampered backup ledger causes restore to be refused.
15. Run existing tests to ensure no regression; the added functionality must not break current flows.
16. Update any TypeScript type definitions or barrel exports to include new types.
17. Ensure all storage access uses the existing Store abstraction (append‑only for ledger, no overwrites except on delete‑all which clears the ledger and starts a new chain).

18. Follow security guidelines: all hashing uses the noble implementation, no custom crypto; ledger entries are encrypted via Store; no path traversal when serving files; verifyBackup rejects tampered ledger before mutating state.

requirements.text: Keep every existing screen, flow, the local‑first design and the current look.
Keep all existing tests passing.
Never modify src/lib/crypto.ts (it is locked).

Use the SHA‑256 implementation from @noble/hashes ^2.4.0 by importing { sha256 } from '@noble/hashes/sha2.js' and { bytesToHex, utf8ToBytes } from '@noble/hashes/utils.js' and do not write your own hashing function.

When a receipt is created, src/lib/ledger.ts must append a ledger entry object with fields: seq, at (ISO‑8601 timestamp), kind set to "receipt.created", recordId, data containing the full receipt content after creation, prevHash, and hash.
When a receipt is edited, src/lib/ledger.ts must append a ledger entry with kind "receipt.corrected" containing the new receipt content in data and linking via prevHash to the previous entry.
When a receipt is deleted, src/lib/ledger.ts must append a ledger entry with kind "receipt.deleted" containing the last receipt content in data and linking via prevHash.
When a mileage entry is created, src/lib/ledger.ts must append a ledger entry with kind "mileage.created" and the fields seq, at, recordId, data, prevHash, hash.
When a mileage entry is edited, src/lib/ledger.ts must append a ledger entry with kind "mileage.corrected" containing the new mileage content in data and linking via prevHash.
When a mileage entry is deleted, src/lib/ledger.ts must append a ledger entry with kind "mileage.deleted" containing the last mileage content in data and linking via prevHash.

On the first launch after the update, the app must create exactly one "imported" ledger entry for each pre‑existing receipt and each pre‑existing mileage entry, using kind "imported", data with the original record content, at set to the import date, and recordId referencing the original record.
The "imported" entries added on first launch must be added only once per existing receipt and mileage entry.
All ledger entries must be stored encrypted through the Store module and must never be rewritten or removed, preserving an append‑only storage model.
The only operation that may clear the ledger and start a new empty ledger is the "Delete all data" action.
The hash for each ledger entry must be calculated as bytesToHex(sha256(utf8ToBytes(canonicalJson))) where canonicalJson is a deterministic JSON serialization of all entry fields except the hash.
The first ledger entry must have its prevHash field set to a 64‑character string of zeros ("0" repeated 64 times).
For every ledger entry after the first, its prevHash field must equal the hash field of the immediately preceding ledger entry, forming a hash chain.

Implement a function verifyLedger(store) that decrypts all stored ledger entries, recomputes each entry's hash and prevHash linkage, and returns an object { ok: boolean, entries: LedgerEntry[], firstBadSeq?: number, reason?: string }.

If verifyLedger finds a mismatch, it must set ok to false, set firstBadSeq to the sequence number of the first corrupted entry, and include a reason string describing the type of corruption (e.g., "hash mismatch", "prevHash mismatch", "missing entry").
verifyLedger must be callable from the Settings screen and from the backup‑restore routine.

Add a History view reachable from each receipt’s detail/edit screen that lists the original ledger entry for that receipt followed by all "receipt.corrected" entries, ordered from oldest to newest (newest last).
Add a History view reachable from each mileage/trip detail screen that lists the original "mileage.created" entry followed by all "mileage.corrected" entries, ordered oldest to newest.
Each entry shown in a History view must display the entry’s date and time taken from the at field in a human‑readable format.
The Settings screen must show the ledger status text "Verified · N entries · intact" when verifyLedger returns ok true, where N is the total number of ledger entries.
When verifyLedger returns ok false, the Settings screen must display a clear warning that records may have been altered and must include the sequence number (or identifier) of the first bad entry.

When exporting data to CSV or PDF, the export file must end with a verification line formatted as "<entryCount>,<headHash>,<verificationCode>" where entryCount is the total number of ledger entries at export time, headHash is the hash of the latest ledger entry, and verificationCode is defined in R27.
The verificationCode must be computed as the first 12 hexadecimal characters of SHA‑256 over the export content excluding the verification line, concatenated with the headHash.

After each CSV or PDF export, src/lib/ledger.ts must append a ledger entry of kind "export.created" with fields: format ("CSV" or "PDF"), code (the verificationCode), entries (the ledger entry count at export time), and headHash (the hash of the latest ledger entry).
The Settings screen must contain a "Verify an export" action that allows the user to either pick an exported CSV file via a file picker or manually type a verification code printed on a PDF export.

When a CSV file is selected, the app must recompute the verificationCode from the file contents without its verification line, locate a matching "export.created" ledger entry, and report whether the code matches an export made by this app.

When a verification code is typed (e.g., from a PDF), the app must locate a matching "export.created" ledger entry and, if found, report the export date and the number of ledger entries at export time.
The export verification result must indicate whether the CSV file has been altered after export (i.e., whether the computed code differs from the stored code).
The export verification result must indicate whether any receipt or mileage records have been corrected or deleted after the export (by checking for ledger entries after the export’s headHash).
If the computed or typed verification code does not correspond to any "export.created" ledger entry, the app must report that the code is unknown and not from this app.
Backups must include the complete encrypted ledger (all ledger entries).
When restoring from a backup, the restore routine must call verifyLedger on the restored ledger before applying any restored data.
If verifyLedger returns ok false for a backup, the restore routine must abort the restore and must not replace any existing data.
If a backup fails verification, the app must display a friendly error message informing the user that the backup appears tampered.
If a restored backup does not contain a ledger (e.g., an older backup), the restore process must import each restored receipt and mileage entry as a new "imported" ledger entry.

Create a unit test that constructs two ledger entries, verifies that the second entry’s hash equals bytesToHex(sha256(utf8ToBytes(canonicalJson))) of its fields, and asserts that the second entry’s prevHash matches the first entry’s hash.
Create a unit test that mutates a field of an existing ledger entry, runs verifyLedger, and asserts that ok is false, firstBadSeq points to the mutated entry, and reason indicates a field change.
Create a unit test that removes a ledger entry from storage, runs verifyLedger, and asserts that verification fails with firstBadSeq set to the missing entry’s sequence number.
Create a unit test that swaps the order of two ledger entries, runs verifyLedger, and asserts that verification fails with firstBadSeq set to the first out‑of‑order entry.
Create a unit test that changes the prevHash of a ledger entry to an incorrect value, runs verifyLedger, and asserts that verification fails with an appropriate reason.
Create a unit test that creates a receipt, edits it, and then checks that both a "receipt.created" entry and a "receipt.corrected" entry exist in the ledger.
Create a unit test that simulates the first launch after the update and verifies that each pre‑existing receipt and mileage record receives exactly one "imported" ledger entry.
Create a unit test that generates a CSV export, reads the file, extracts the verification line, and asserts that the entryCount, headHash, and verificationCode match the ledger state at export time.
Create a unit test that modifies a CSV export file by changing a single character, runs the export verification routine, and asserts that verification fails indicating the file was altered.
Create a unit test that after a CSV export performs a receipt correction, runs the export verification routine, and asserts that the result reports that records have been corrected since the export.
Create a unit test that generates a PDF export, records the printed verification code, and confirms that an "export.created" ledger entry with that code exists.
Create a unit test that provides an unknown verification code to the export verification routine and asserts that the result reports the code as not from this app.
Create a unit test that backs up the app, restores from that backup, runs verifyLedger on the restored data, and asserts that verification succeeds and the restored ledger matches the original.
Create a unit test that tampers with a backup’s ledger (e.g., flips a bit in an entry), attempts a restore, and asserts that the restore is aborted and that a friendly error is shown.
Update ui_flow.json so that the primary flow for editing a receipt includes a step that opens the new History view and displays any correction entries.
Update ui_flow.json so that the primary flow includes a step to open Settings and display the ledger status text "Verified · N entries · intact" when verification succeeds.
